status_summary: Two parts are operative or advancing and one is largely blocked in court. DHS published a final rule on 2025-12-29, effective 2026-02-27, replacing the random H-1B cap lottery with a selection weighted toward higher-skilled and higher-paid beneficiaries, starting with the FY2027 registration season. The Labor Department proposed on 2026-03-27 to raise all four prevailing-wage levels (Level I from about the 17th to the 34th percentile, Level IV from the 67th to the 88th); the text keeps four levels, so it does not eliminate the two lowest as the Mandate asks, and the rule is not final. Proclamation 10973 (signed 2025-09-19) required a 100,000 dollar payment for H-1B workers abroad, and Proclamation 11069 (signed 2026-09-18) extended it to 2027-09-21 with the payment unchanged. Courts have split on the payment: a D.D.C. court upheld it in December 2025 (on appeal); a D. Mass. court (State of California v. Mullin, No. 25-13829, Judge Sorokin) vacated the implementing policy on 2026-06-08, holding the payment an unauthorized tax and the policy issued without notice and comment and beyond statutory authority, then paused its order on 2026-06-12 pending a stay request, and the First Circuit declined a stay in July 2026 (both per CUPA-HR); and an N.D. Cal. court vacated implementing policies for both proclamations on 2026-09-30 until notice-and-comment rulemaking is done. DHS also proposed on 2026-08-25 a 103,265 dollar fee on cap-subject petitions (comments closed 2026-09-24), and Executive Order 14431 (2026-09-18) directs agencies to coordinate on H-1B integrity and layoff-related review without changing wage levels.

timeline.event: Proclamation 10973 restricts entry of H-1B workers unless the employer pays 100,000 dollars, effective 2025-09-21 for 12 months unless extended, with DHS waiver authority.

The U.S. District Court for D.C. upholds the proclamation in Chamber of Commerce v. DHS; the Chamber appeals to the D.C. Circuit, where the case is pending (December 2025; day not given, first of month used).
DHS publishes the final rule on weighted selection for cap-subject H-1B registrations, favoring higher-skilled and higher-paid beneficiaries, effective 2026-02-27 for the FY2027 registration season.

Labor Department proposes to raise the four prevailing-wage levels for H-1B, PERM and related programs to the 34th, 52nd, 70th and 88th percentiles (from about the 17th, 34th, 50th and 67th); comments closed 2026-05-26.

Judge Leo Sorokin (D. Mass.), in State of California v. Mullin (No. 25-13829-LTS), grants summary judgment to twenty states and vacates in its entirety the agency policy implementing Proclamation 10973's 100,000 dollar payment. The court holds that the payment is a tax that the proclamation's statutory authorities (INA 212(f) and 215(a)) do not delegate, and that the policy is a legislative rule issued without notice and comment, exceeds statutory authority and is arbitrary and capricious; it grants no separate injunction. The government appeals to the First Circuit on 2026-06-11 (per Ogletree), the district court pauses its order on 2026-06-12 (per CUPA-HR), and CUPA-HR reports the First Circuit declined a stay in July 2026.
timeline.source: U.S. District Court for the District of Massachusetts (Memorandum and Order, Doc. 106)

timeline.event: DHS proposes a 103,265 dollar filing fee for all cap-subject H-1B petitions, in addition to other fees; comments closed 2026-09-24.

Proclamation 11069 extends the entry restriction to 2027-09-21 with the 100,000 dollar payment unchanged and DHS waiver authority; Executive Order 14431, signed the same day, directs State, Labor and DHS to coordinate on H-1B integrity and consider employer layoffs.

A federal court in the Northern District of California vacates agency policies implementing the 100,000 dollar payment under both Proclamation 10973 and Proclamation 11069 and bars enforcement until notice-and-comment rulemaking is done; whether the order is stayed or appealed was not reported.
